prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1284; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. Driver 2 was stopped in traffic when the front of Driver 1's vehicle struck the rear of Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 reported a shoulder injury and said the impact was the cause. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel when officers arrived, and a Passenger in the front seat was also present and confirmed being in the vehicle at the time of the crash. Driver 2 gave a statement consistent with Driver 1's account of how the collision occurred, and two independent witnesses at the scene described the same sequence of events. Officers photographed both vehicles. The rear damage to Driver 2's vehicle and the front damage to Driver 1's vehicle line up with the reported speed and angle of impact, and the officers observed no prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 was checked at the scene and transported for evaluation. The shoulder complaint is a common result of a collision of this type. Records confirm Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
